machine: RX 9070 XT (RDNA4), Mesa 26.3.1 RADV, CachyOS, GE-Proton11-14, vkd3d-proton master

header.meaning: 100 % in every row means every part the title uses is implemented and verified on Mesa; it is the target, not a guarantee, and correctness is checked by runs, not counts.
header.where: Measured on 25 Nov 2026, build 5fca579b, RX 9070 XT (RDNA4) / Mesa 26.3.1 RADV. Diagnostics builds. No other GPU has been tried, and every number below comes from that one card.
notes: Every percentage is a share of a **named set that was counted** on this machine: an import table, a shader archive, a frame of recorded work. None of them is a share of the title as a whole, and the sets overlap (a program in the shader archive is not a distinct piece of the port).

**Implemented** is what our code does today; **verified** is how much of that a run has shown working. They are separate columns because a decoder can claim an opcode that no run has proved. An em dash means that column was not counted for that row.
The counts are taken from files the user supplies; nothing from them is stored in this repository, and no title, program or asset name appears here.

A set can be complete without being ours: every import of the title **resolves** (0 missing), but 427 of the 587 are Wine (Proton) and 72 belong to the title's own libraries. The System APIs area shows both numbers side by side, and only the 88 HLE ones are code this project wrote.

areas.title: Pipelines
areas.summary: A draw cannot run until its pipeline exists on the host. The world set can be built entirely offline, and the pre-bake list covers most of what the title asks for in a session; what is left is created while the title waits for it.

rows.label: Pipelines the title asks for, covered by the pre-bake list
rows.note: 1,785 of the 2,601 keys the title's own early list names can be built from the saved library

rows.label: Late creates per frame in a world run
rows.note: programs dropped while their pipeline is made, summed over a whole run

foot: The pre-bake list is the union of the early-pipeline key list and the warm pipeline library the title saved itself; the gap is what a session creates on demand.
One program takes 3.6 s to compile alone, so the pre-bake must not schedule it last.

areas.title: Mesa reach (compiled offline, not run)
areas.summary: Whether the world shader set compiles for a GPU family's Mesa driver, without that GPU. Mesa's noop drm-shim fakes each chip, so RADV and ANV build every pipeline with that family's ISA and limits. Every AMD generation up to ours compiles the whole set except Vega, whose mesh-shader programs abort the driver. On Intel, Arc B builds the whole set, while Arc A and Xe-LPG each miss one program on the stub's own gap. This is a compile result: only RDNA4 has actually been run.

rows.label: AMD families whose whole world set compiles offline
rows.note: 4 of 5 AMD families compile the whole set through the noop shim (Mesa driver, no GPU)

rows.label: Arc B (Xe2): world programs that build pipelines offline
rows.note: 751 of 751 build a pipeline through ANV and Mesa's Intel noop shim; none is refused; median 35 ms per program

rows.label: Arc A (DG2): world programs that build pipelines offline
rows.note: 750 of 751 build a pipeline; the one miss is the stub's gap (Unknown drm_i915_query_item), not a compiler error; median 78 ms per program

rows.label: Xe-LPG: world programs that build pipelines offline
rows.note: 750 of 751 build a pipeline; the one miss is the same stub gap; median 69 ms per program

rows.label: Vega (gfx900): world programs that compile offline
rows.note: 82 of 751 abort the driver: every mesh-shader program, and GFX9 has no mesh shader support in RADV

rows.label: Families with a run, not just a compile
rows.note: only our card: every other family has compiled pipelines and no run

foot: Sources: `family-matrix-20261125-134909-2134785.tsv` (AMD, five families + the real card as control), `family-matrix-20261125-140636-2410746.tsv` (Intel: dg2, bmg, mtl) and `family-matrix-20261125-141256-2481125.tsv` (re-check of gfx1201 and acm: 751/751 and 750/751, the same result); the shim column for our own family matches the real-GPU column exactly, so the harness does not change the answer.

Compiled offline is not run. On RDNA1 all 82 mesh programs create, yet RADV does not advertise `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` there, so a program that uses mesh, barycentric or ray query at draw time needs the game's own fallback path.

Intel: ANV needs `libvulkan_intel.so` plus Mesa's Intel noop shim from the same build; both were built for this run. The one program that fails on dg2 and mtl is the same class, and it stops on the stub's `drm_i915_query_item` gap, not on a shader the compiler refused. Nothing Intel has been run on a card.

areas.title: Performance
areas.summary: Speed is measured at one fixed scene, the only figure compared between builds, against the console's 30 fps target. The port is far from it, and the card is idle for most of the frame because the CPU side is the cost.

rows.label: Fixed test scene vs the 30 fps console target
rows.note: 1.6 fps median at the window scene of the last recorded run, compared only with rows of the same scene

rows.label: Card busy share of the frame
rows.note: by our own clock count; the rest is the title's CPU work and our copies

rows.label: Time to the world
rows.note: from launch to the first world frame; the pre-bake should cut it

foot: fps is the median of samples at the `window` scene, compared only between rows with the same scene label; `world_fps` from other runs mixes cutscenes and is never published.
The frame is split as: title CPU work, our copies, then the card. Our copies are 98-111 ms of a 515-540 ms frame in the measured world run.

method.how: the title image's import table is scanned by our own census tool, which marks each function as answered by one of our HLE modules, passed through to Wine, exported by the title's own images, or missing; a world run prints the same split on its `bound` line, which is the verified column. Only the HLE column is code we wrote

`victory translate` over the whole shader archive for the translated and emitted counts, and over the 751-program world set with dxil-spirv, `spirv-val` and a real RADV pipeline for the verified column
the backend's per-frame log lines in a world run, summed by drop reason; the D3D12 calls are the title's call list against the presence of each name in the backend's sources
the offline world-set run (cold and warm Mesa cache), the title's own saved pipeline keys, and the `without a host pipeline` lines of a world run
run verdicts and the picture notes; a feature is never called working without a frame that shows it
the five-family offline matrix through Mesa's amdgpu noop shim, plus the real card as control; a family counts only when all of its pipelines compile
the fixed-scene runner's median fps and the launch-to-world time from the loader's own timestamps
